question: The danger space of the deep neck (space 4, between alar and prevertebral fascia) extends from the skull base to the diaphragm and therefore provides a direct anatomical conduit for infection to track into the posterior mediastinum, enabling descending necrotising mediastinitis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is anatomically accurate. The danger space (space 4) between the alar and prevertebral layers of deep cervical fascia does extend from skull base to diaphragm, and spread of infection through it causes the feared complication of descending necrotising mediastinitis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The danger space is so named precisely because it extends from the skull base to the diaphragm without fascial barriers, providing an unobstructed pathway for infection to descend into the posterior mediastinum. Descending necrotising mediastinitis carries a mortality rate of 40-50% even with prompt surgical drainage.
